<!-- An adversarial review of explorations/coordinator/array-design.md (203 lines, commits c227cbe55 and d55aa91a6 of 2026-09-19), written 2026-09-20 on Pavol's permission by a worker that did not write the design and had not read it before. Read against the sources the brief names: POSITIONS.md (2026-09-16 and 2026-09-19 onward), FACTS.md, the map, the scalar-extension review, the array work brief, the specification, and the code the design points at; and, added by the coordinator while the review was under way, reviews/nat-checking-plan.md (the earlier plan for teaching the checker nat parameters, itself unreviewed) with reviews/template-checking-plan.md as its sibling, against which section 1b judges the design's nat rungs. Every claim below carries a file:line or a probe capture; the probes and their captures are in explorations/compiler-probes/array-design-review/ (README there). Tree at fa8414d69. Findings most serious first; then the decisions that are Pavol's, each as what-we-do / what-it-changes with a labelled default; then the verdict. One line per paragraph. -->

# Review of the array design for the compiled world

## 0. What was checked and how

The design's own citations were opened: every line number in §1, §2, §4c, §5, §6a-§6e and §8 was read in the tree, and the two rulings were read in `POSITIONS.md:40`. Where the design says "unprobed" or "not measured", or where a claim depends on what the checker does rather than on what the interpreter does, a probe was run: five Fortress programs through `fortress compile` under a private cache (one also through the interpreter), and two Java models beside the kernel models of `perf-probes/kernels/java`. Nothing under `default_repository/`, `Library/` or `ProjectFortress/` was touched.

The standard applied is the one in the brief: finish what the designers intended, judged by the July 2012 draft and the breadcrumbs in all three sources of truth (specification, interpreter and its library, compiler and its prelude); storage is `double[]`, unboxed; sizes are `nat` parameters and the two forks are taken together; extensions go into the standard library in the library's own patterns; and the measuring stick is one program, microGPT compiled and running fast.

## 1. Findings

### Decisive 1. The design keeps the model's unsized static types and never checks the model's applications against a static checker; as written, nothing in microGPT and none of the three kernels passes the type checker, whatever the storage is

What the design says. §3: "every constructor takes a run-time size and returns the unsized `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]` or `Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]`"; §6d, default: "the run-time-sized factory returns the unsized `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]` as it already does in the model … and only literal and symbol sizes get sized classes"; §6c: the minimal checker "covers all 81 and all of microGPT's" declarations; §8: the second rung times "`kdot` compiled over a native `dot`".

What the model is. `rmsn(x: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\])` computes `x DOT x` (`run-c4/src/MicroGptFlat.fss:27`); `DOT` exists only on `Vector[\T,n\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2264-2265`, and the api `.fsi:1508`); `FlatArrays` declares no `DOT`. `view(p, i)` returns `Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]` (`:45`), `wq^T` needs `Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]` (`:23`), and `x1 wq^T` (`:58`) is the library's juxtaposition on two `Matrix` (`.fss:2625-2627`); `x1` comes from `rows`, which returns `Array` (`FlatArrays.fss:139`). `diag(vm / nv)` (`:63`) passes an `Array` where `diag` takes `Vector[\RR64,s\]` (`FlatArrays.fss:41`); `gather(wte, ids)` (`:57`) passes the `Array` from `view` where `gather` takes `Matrix`; `rows(rmsn, x)` (`:57`) passes the `Array` from `gather + gather` where `rows` takes `Matrix`. The kernels are the same: `kdot.fss` writes `x DOT y` on two `vec(…)` results typed `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]` (`FlatArrays.fss:14`); `kmat.fss` writes `a b` on two `mat(…)` results; `krows.fss` writes `rows(rmsn, m)` on a `mat(…)` result.

Why it runs on the interpreter. `array[\E\](n)` reflects `n` into a nat and calls `array1[\E,n\]()` (`.fss:1927-1934`), which selects `vector[\T,s0\]()` for any `Number` by `typecase` (`:2240-2244`), so the run-time object behind every `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]` in the model is a `__DefaultVector[\RR64,n\]`, a `Vector`, and the interpreter dispatches on the run-time object; the static type is never consulted (FACTS, execution model: the checker "runs only on the compile path"). The same holds for the views: `view` calls `viewN(p, off, reflect(nr), reflect(nc))` (`FlatArrays.fss:60-62`), where `reflect` returns `NatParam` (`LibraryBuiltin/NatReflect.fsi`) and `viewN` takes `N[\r\]`; only the run-time object is an `N[\16\]`.

What the checker does with it. Probe `p3_static_dispatch.fss`, no `nat` in it so nothing else can be what fails: a trait `Vec[\T\] extends Arr[\T\]`, an object under `Vec[\RR64\]`, a function on two `Vec[\RR64\]`, and a call on a value whose static type is `Arr[\RR64\]`. Compile path: `(Vec[\RR64\], Vec[\RR64\])->RR64 is not applicable to an argument of type (Arr[\RR64\], Arr[\RR64\])`, exit 255 (`p3_static_dispatch.compile.out`); interpreter, same file: `p3 9.0` (`p3_static_dispatch.interp.out`). As an operator the refusal is identical and lists the prelude's scalar `DOT` overloads beside the user's (`p3b_static_dispatch_opr.compile.out`).

Where the first compiled microGPT fails, then. Before the model: `FlatArrays.fss:62`, `viewN(p, off, reflect(nr), reflect(nc))`, because `NatParam` is not `N[\r\]` statically and the checker cannot infer `r` from a run-time object. Then `MicroGptFlat.fss:27` on `x DOT x`, and after that nearly every line of `step` (`:57-70`). The design's own second-rung measurement, `kdot` through a native `dot`, cannot happen as written: `kdot.fss:15` is `x DOT y` on two unsized `Array`s.

Why this is decisive. The two rulings of 2026-09-19 (`POSITIONS.md:38, 40`) are "the model's text is the notation" and "nat sizes are central, not sidestepped"; on the compile path these two collide on every operator application in the model, because the model's text carries sizes only in its run-time objects. The design says "the checker sees the library's own types; the model's `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]`, `Vector[\RR64,s\]`, `Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]` resolve as written" (§4c); the types resolve, the applications do not. That collision is not named anywhere in the 203 lines, and it is the first decision Pavol has to take (§2, decision D), not a repair a rung can make.

### Decisive 2. The default for "what implements the sized traits over the store" has no checked mechanism on this path; the checker refuses it, including through the library's own selection idiom

What the design says. §4c and §7 question 2, default: `__DefaultVector[\T, nat s0\]` "keeps its shape and its `mem` field is the `RR64` store for `RR64`, `FZZ32Vector` for `ZZ32`, the boxed store otherwise, chosen by the factory from the run-time type tag … it needs one probe and no loader change, and it is the library's own structure"; "a native helper behind `array1[\T, nat s0\]()` can return the `double[]` store when `T`'s tag is `FRR64` and the boxed store otherwise".

What the probes say. `p1_monostore.fss`: a generic `Arr[\T\]`, a monomorphic `DStore extends Arr[\RR64\]`, and `mk[\T\](x: T): Arr[\T\] = DStore()`. Refused: `Function body has type DStore, but declared return type is Arr[\T\]` (`p1_monostore.compile.out`). `p1b_typecase.fss`, the library's own idiom from `array1` (`FortressLibrary.fss:2240-2244`), `typecase w of () -> RR64 => DStore() else => BStore[\T\](x) end`: refused, `Function body has type OR(DStore,BStore[\T\]), but declared return type is Arr[\T\]` (`p1b_typecase.compile.out`). The library's `array1` passes the interpreter because nothing checks it, and would pass the checker only because both of its arms (`vector[\T,s0\]()`, `PrimitiveArray[\T,s0\]()`) stay generic in `T`; a `double[]` store is not generic in `T`, which is the whole point of it.

What "the library's own structure" would have to become. A generic object cannot have a field whose type changes with `T`; `mem: PrimitiveArray[\T,s0\]` is one type. So the shape is one monomorphic storing object per native element type (`__RR64Vector[\nat s0\]() extends Vector[\RR64,s0\]` with `mem: RR64Store`) beside the generic boxed one, and the problem moves to the factory `vector[\T extends Number, nat s0\]()`, which must return the monomorphic object for `T = RR64` inside a body the checker types with `T` abstract; the probes show it cannot. A foreign helper cannot be generic (`import java` binds static methods with fixed types, `CompilerBuiltin.fss:300-306`); a second factory name per element type is the library's pattern for `array1`/`vector` (`.fss:2251`) but does not make `vector[\RR64,16\]()` produce the store; a code-generator special case in the manner of `NamingCzar`'s hand-implemented types (`NamingCzar.java:538-553`) is a `.java` change. Every route is a `.java` rung; "no loader change" is not one of them.

The branch the design dismissed is the team's. §7's second branch, "the loader picks a `double[]` template per instantiation", is set aside as "nothing of it exists, and the instantiater's only tool is name substitution". The team's breadcrumbs point there: `compiler/optimization/Unbox.java:12-19` lists as case 1 "primitive. ZZ{8,16,32,64}, RR{32,64}, Boolean" and as case 3 "unboxed fields"; the expando stub `if (false) { // Here will go all the magic expando-stuff. }` is in the loader (`InstantiatingClassloader.java:168-172`); the JVM paper's stamping by upper bound (`MethodMapping.tex:134`) is the mechanism that would be specialised. `PLAN.md` step 5 says of this exact item "the probe on generic instantiation in the class loader comes first"; the design's probe 1 shows what the loader does today, not whether it can select, and the plan's probe was not run. Our own roadmap's A2 ("selected from the element type carried at run time. Scala's `Array[Double]` via class tags", `performance-roadmap.md:40`) is the design's default; the team's direction is the other branch. Which precedent wins is Pavol's (§2, decision A).

### Decisive 3. The second reserved fork, the library route, is closed by default in §7, against the ruling as it was applied the same evening

## 2. The seven questions, answered by finding

**Q1, finish or redesign.** It finishes the specification's shape: the sized family `Array k[T, 0, n0, …]` over a generic array (`aggregate.tex:130-136`), both factories (`arrays-distributed.tex:42-48`), a linear store under a structure (`:18-22`, `future.tex:42`), sizes in types (`nutshell.tex:85-86`), and the checker doing what the interpreter's `unifyStaticArg` does (`IntNat.java:127-147`). It departs in six places: the storing objects are rewritten, not copied (finding 5, unnamed); the run-time-sized factory's dynamic half, that an `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]` is a `Vector` underneath, is dropped (§6d, named as "the one library pattern the compiled world does not reproduce", but its consequence for the model is not, finding 1); natives in place of the team's generated-code unboxing (finding 4, half named); store selection by run-time tag, our roadmap's A2, in place of the team's `Unbox`/expando direction (finding 2, unnamed); a third library text in the compiler world in place of the spec's Core/Standard split and the ruling's "the standard library" (finding 3, unnamed); and the compiler world's own precedent, the unsized rank-polymorphic `ZZ32Vector`, set aside (§4b, named).

**Q2, the defaults.** Finding 2 (store selection: refuted by probe, alternatives all `.java`, precedent points the other way), finding 4 (loops: measured to buy nothing on the model's shapes, no precedent), finding 7 (unconstrained nats: unsafe side, and the real problem is an api/component mismatch). The smaller defaults: the nat also as a run-time field is right and forced (finding 5); the run-time-sized factory returning the unsized `Array` is what breaks the model (finding 1); one shadow session before the checker edit is right and should widen to five probes (§7 below). Which are Pavol's: all three large ones and the run-time-size one; the shadow session is the worker's.

**Q3, the nat plan.** The Scala side is consistent with itself: `staticInstantiation` already substitutes `IntRef` (`STypesUtil.scala:670`), `staticArgsMatchStaticParams` already accepts an `IntArg` for `KindNat` (`:742-747, 767-772`), self-types are built with `IntArg(IntRef)` for nat kinds (`:338-339, 352-353`), and the equality hole is one line (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:332`). Unsound or unproven: the crash is in Java replacer composition (finding 6); "no arithmetic" refuses three library objects (finding 5); the export checker meets an arity mismatch (finding 7); nothing in the plan or the design touches code generation or the runtime for a nat argument, which the first sized object needs (finding 6). Smallest rung that proves or refutes it: the shadow session with `NatInfer1`, `NatObject1`, `NatValue1`, `XXXNatMismatch1` as the design lists them, plus `NatExtends1` (`object V[\nat n\]() extends S[\n\] end` instantiated as `V[\3\]()`, through code generation and a run) and `NatStore1` (a generic factory returning a monomorphic object, the probe `p1_monostore.fss` as it stands). Dead ends: the `TypeArg`/`IntArg` confusion pervasive in the Java front end; a nat needing a runtime RTTI kind; the checker refusing the library's own storing objects with no arithmetic rule the spec permits.

**Q4, `double[]` under the generic trait.** Stamping cannot produce a `[D` field; the design's probe 1 settles that and the map already said it (`map/README.md:43`). The `ZZ32Vector` precedent proves that a hand-written class can implement a trait's `DefaultTraitMethods`, be a `NamingCzar` special type, and reach Java natives through `import java`, and `FZZ32` proves it under instantiated generic supertraits (finding 9). It does not prove unboxed traffic (probe 2, and `KDotStore`), per-instantiation representation, or anything about nats. The route the design proposes for selecting the store is refused by the checker (finding 2); the route that could give unboxed storage per element type under one generic trait is the loader/code-generator one, which `PLAN.md` step 5 says to probe first and which the design dismissed unprobed.

**Q5, the two preludes.** The compiler world, said in §4c and §7's last paragraph, and no more than said: what it costs (a second algebra, ~1,200 lines of array text, two library texts from then on, the interpreter's copy never checked) and what it forecloses (the library route, a reserved fork) are absent (finding 3).

**Q6, the 26 operations and the three kernels.** As written, none is reachable from the model's text and none of the kernels compiles, for the reason of finding 1; the first failure is `FlatArrays.fss:62`, the second `MicroGptFlat.fss:27`. On values that are statically sized (literal sizes, `vector[\RR64,16\]()`), the design serves: the 14 elementwise maps (declared over `Array[\RR64,I\]`, bodies boxed per element under the question-3 default), the library's products and `Diag`, `transpose` of a `Matrix`. It cannot serve as written: `view`, `row`, `row3`, `heads`, `unheads`, `plane` (run-time shapes through `reflect`), `rows` in all four shapes (takes `Matrix`, returns `Array`, so one `rows` cannot feed the next), `gather`, `pick`, `onehot` where the argument is a view's result, and the batched product on `heads`' results. The kernels: `kdot` and `kmat` need `vec`/`mat` to return sized types or `DOT`/juxtaposition to be declared over `Array`; `krows` needs both and `rows`.

**Q7, order and stop.** The first gated rung should not be the checker rung until a shadow rung with no gate has answered five questions (§7 below); the checker rung is right as the first gated rung only if the shadow says the crash is in Scala. The stop conditions are in §7.

## 3. Decisions that are Pavol's

Each as what we do, what it changes, the alternatives, and a labelled default that can be accepted without reading the argument; the argument is in §1.

### Decision A. What puts `double[]` under the library's sized traits

What we do: choose the mechanism by which `Vector[\RR64,16\]` gets a `double[]` store while `Vector[\T,16\]` for other `T` gets a boxed one.

What it changes: which `.java` rung the array work needs first, and whether the library's generic factories keep their text.

Alternatives. (A1) The design's default, a factory selecting by run-time type tag under one generic storing object: refused by the checker (finding 2); to keep it, a code-generator special case for the factory, a `.java` rung with no team precedent. (A2) The team's direction: the code generator and loader give a stamped `PrimitiveArray⟦FRR64,n⟧` a `double[]` field, `Unbox.java` case 1 plus the expando stub; the library's text stays as it is; the largest change, in the loader and `CodeGen`, and `PLAN.md` step 5's own first probe. (A3) Monomorphic storing objects per native element type (`__RR64Vector[\nat s0\]`) beside the generic boxed one, with a monomorphic factory name per element type in the manner of `array1`/`vector` (`.fss:2251`); typed cleanly, no code-generator change, but the model then names `rr64vector`, not `vector`, and the generic `Vector[\T,s0\]` is boxed for every `T` including `RR64` unless the user calls the right factory.

Default: probe A2 first (one shadow experiment, `next-climb.md` §3b's first item), because it is the team's breadcrumb and `PLAN.md`'s order; A3 is the fallback that needs no `.java`; A1 is closed by the probe unless Pavol wants the special case.

### Decision B. Where loops run unboxed

What we do: choose between Java natives per whole-array operation and unboxing `RR64` by static type in generated code.

What it changes: whether the ruling "it cannot be boxed" holds for the model (views, lambdas, `rows`) or only for whole-array operations on stores; and the size of the code-generator work.

Alternatives. (B1) Natives first, the design's default: measured at 8.9×/6.6× primitive on the model's shapes (finding 4), the same as boxed storage; helps `p DOT p` and Adam only; no precedent. (B2) Unboxing by static type first (roadmap A1, `Unbox.java` case 1): `D` locals, `daload`/`dastore`, `dadd`/`dmul` wherever the checker's type is `RR64`; the library's own Fortress loops (`fill`, `map`, `Vector.dot`) become unboxed without natives; every rung `.java` under the full gate; the team's precedent. (B3) Both, in the order B2 for element access and arithmetic, natives only where a whole-array kernel beats the JIT (a measured residue, not a default).

Default: B2, because it is the only alternative under which the ruling is true of the model, and the kernel measurement in the array rung is then `kdot` in Fortress against `KDotPrim`, not against a native.

### Decision C. Which library the array layer and the model's operations go into

What we do: choose between growing the compiler world (`CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerBuiltin`, `CompilerAlgebra`) with a copy of the array layer and the algebra above `Number`, and making the interpreter's library (`FortressLibrary`) the prelude the compiler checks.

What it changes: whether the standard library exists once or twice from here on; whether yesterday's commit to `FortressLibrary.fss` and this design's rungs land in the same file; the 92 tower errors and 108 native bindings of the library route (FACTS) against the second copy of about 1,200 lines plus the algebra.

Alternatives. (C1) The compiler world, the design's default. (C2) The library route, `PLAN.md`'s reserved fork: the interpreter's library becomes the checked prelude; the 92 errors are classified first (`next-climb.md` §3b's last item, "one probe"). (C3) One text, two bindings: the array layer and algebra written once in `Library/` in Fortress, with the native bindings the only per-world file (`NativeArray.fss` with `builtinPrimitive` for the interpreter, a compiler-world twin with `import java`); whether the two worlds can share a prelude file is unprobed.

Default: none can be labelled; this is the reserved fork and it is Pavol's. The cheapest fact before deciding is the classification of the 92 errors.

### Decision D. The model's static types

What we do: decide how `MicroGptFlat.fss` and `FlatArrays.fss` are typed for a static checker, given that today their values are statically unsized and their operations are declared on sized types (finding 1).

What it changes: the model's text, or the vocabulary's declarations, or the compile path.

Alternatives. (D1) The model carries sizes in its types as the specification intends (`makeVector`, `trait-parameters.tex:94-97`): `step` and its helpers become generic in `nat` parameters, the hyperparameters become static arguments, and every `Array[\RR64,…\]` in the model becomes a `Vector`/`Matrix`/`Array3` with nats; the ruling of `POSITIONS.md:38` requires the diff to be shown before it is built. (D2) The vocabulary is declared over the unsized `Array[\RR64,I\]` and the products the model uses (`DOT`, juxtaposition, `rows`, `gather`, `diag`) are added over `Array` beside the library's sized ones; the model's text is unchanged; the sized products and the shape check are then not what the model exercises, which is the sidestep the second ruling refuses. (D3) A compile-path `reflect`: a native that asks the loader for `N⟦n⟧` by name at run time, which the team's own comment asks for ("we ought to build it in", `NatReflect.fss:39`); it keeps the model's dynamic dispatch but does not make the static types sized, so it does not by itself pass the checker; it is what D1 needs for the run-time-sized parameter vector.

Default: D1 with D3, because both rulings are honoured only there; D2 is the honest alternative if the model's text is to stay byte-identical. The first thing to show Pavol is the D1 diff of `rmsn` and `step`'s signature, not a rung.

### Decision E. The six api declarations with dead nats

What we do: decide what the checker does with `nat m` and `nat p` in `.fsi:1496-1523`, which the component does not have.

What it changes: whether the checker rung touches `Library/` (six api lines) and what an unsolved nat means anywhere.

Alternatives. (E1) Default to 0, the design's: unsafe when the parameter is later used as a value (finding 7), and blind to the api/component shape mismatch. (E2) Unsolved is an error when the nat reaches a type, a name or a value, nothing otherwise (the interpreter's `BottomType` rule); the six declarations pass because their dead parameters reach nothing; the export checker compares by name and reports the extra parameter. (E3) Delete the dead parameters from the api, a sealed-tree library edit flagged at commit, and the export checker then agrees.

Default: E2 in the checker, E3 as the library edit shown to Pavol as a six-line diff; not E1.

### Decision F. What the first gated rung is, and what stops the climb

What we do: run a shadow rung with no gate before the checker rung, answering: where the `VarType`/`IntExpr` crash comes from; what the export checker reports on the six declarations; whether a generic object with a nat argument in `extends` can be stamped and run (`NatExtends1`); whether the store can be selected under the generic factory in any typed way (`NatStore1`, decision A); and whether the loader can be made to select a representation (decision A2). Then the checker rung.

Stop conditions to adopt, each returning to Pavol with the capture: the crash's fix is in a Java front-end class, so the plan's "no Java" and its size are void; a nat argument needs a new RTTI kind in `runtimeSystem/`; the checker refuses every typed route to the store (A1 and A3 both fail); the model cannot be typed without a diff to its lines (decision D not taken); the kernel compiled over the store lands at the `KDotStore` number rather than the `KDotPrim` number, which means the traffic is still boxed.

## 4. Verdict

Unsound as written. The two rulings stand and the shape the design draws from them, sized traits over a native linear store with the checker doing what `unifyStaticArg` does, is the specification's own shape and has the team's breadcrumbs behind it (`future.tex:42`, `arrays-distributed.tex:18-22`, `MethodMapping.tex:142`). But three load-bearing claims fail: the plan cannot compile the program it is measured by, because it keeps the model's unsized static types and the checker resolves statically (finding 1); its default mechanism for putting `double[]` under the generic trait is refused by the checker, and the branch it dismissed is the team's (finding 2); and it closes the second reserved fork in one line (finding 3). It becomes sound only under conditions Pavol sets: decision D taken and its diff shown; decision A taken after the loader probe `PLAN.md` step 5 already orders; decision C taken as the fork it is; decision B taken with the `KDotStore` measurement in view; and the shadow rung and stop conditions of decision F adopted before the first gated rung.

## The library's arrays and algebra

- `Vector[\T extends Number, nat s0\]` and `Matrix[\T extends Number, nat s0, nat s1\]` are the only sized array traits; `Array3[\T, nat b0, nat s0, …\]` carries no algebraic trait (row 292; `FortressLibrary.fsi:1460, 1578, 1652`).
- `Vector` and `Matrix` inherit `+`, `-`, unary `-` and `zero` from `AdditiveGroup`, nothing else; `×` reaches no array by design because juxtaposition is the inner product and the array traits exclude `AnyMultiplicativeRing` (rows 64, 109, 293); a carrier that extends the ring is accepted unchecked, changes juxtaposition to elementwise and breaks `+` (vocabulary review v02, v02b).
- The library's products are declared with shared `nat`s (`Matrix[\T,n,m\]` × `Matrix[\T,m,p\]`, `FortressLibrary.fsi:1508-1516`); C4's own products were not, which is habit; the focused base's `FlatArrays2` states them (twelve declarations including the per-rank elementwise `×` and `/`, 25 of 29 nats agreeing; 39 declarations), and a wrong-shape call is refused at dispatch, uncatchable for an overloaded name (row 83), as a unification error naming the nat for an unoverloaded one (`apl/mg/checks/mismatch_probe.out`).
- Two declarations of one name differing only in the element type, or a rank-specialised declaration beside an index-generic one, are refused at load ("at least one pair of parameters must have excluding types"; `apl/mg/checks/model_run.out.0`, `elemwise_nat_probe.out.0`); two apis' overloads of one name are checked as one family, so two vocabularies cannot stand in one component (`diag_fwd_two_vocabularies_rejected.out.0`).
- The shipped `RR64` does not satisfy the specification's algebraic bound `T extends AdditiveGroup[\T\]` (vocabulary review, probe `v04b_groupbound.out.0`); `T extends Number` is the bound that works for every element type and rank (row 295).
- The library's scalar-extension block for `+ - MIN MAX` over arrays is generic since `02d09a39f` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4511-4521`, `.fsi:2550-2560`); no reshape, plane, gather, outer product or ravel exists in the library (vocabulary review, section A).
- An array is a trait with `get`/`put`; a view is an object implementing it over other storage, the language's own idiom; the library's row slice `m[i,:]` costs 5× a six-line user view; a diagonal as a `Matrix` view costs 13-54× the operator (vocabulary review v20, v07).
- The element type is `Number` only for `Vector`/`Matrix` (row 24); irrelevant to numeric microGPT, decisive for Run B's autodiff value and for APL characters.

content.content:
- 2026-09-19: interpreter performance is irrelevant to every decision — "interpreter of Fortress, which is hundreds times slower than the Python interpreter, is irrelevant for any performance discussions"; "we cannot judge anything performance related in Fortress while we do not have a compiler". No edit to C4 for speed (the tuple-split measurement is an interpreter number only), and no performance decision of any kind until microGPT runs compiled.
- 2026-09-19, on the FlatArrays review's repair that turned `mask + (qh kh^T) / SQRT (1.0 headDim)` into `planeSum(mask, …)`: "NO. That's not Fortress!" The model's text is the notation the project exists for; an operator in it does not become a function call to satisfy the interpreter's overload check. The edit was stopped before it landed. Any repair that would change a line of the model is shown to him as a diff before it is built, and the vocabulary is repaired around the notation, not the other way round.
- 2026-09-19, answering the open question of 2026-09-15 (own tree or the sealed `Library/`): "all the extensions that [microGPT] invented need to go directly to the standard library in the spirit of the standard library." Exclusion "is a practice that is all over the standard library"; whoever extends the library "should study the existing parts of the Fortress library meticulously, and use those patterns for extending the standard library in the native way". No fix is designed from a reading of the specification alone or from a user-side workaround; the library's own practice is the standard.
- 2026-09-19, on `coordinator/array-design.md`'s four questions: storage is `double[]`, unboxed — "we must go to double array for performance. There is again no question about this. If this should have been high performance language, it cannot be boxed." And the `nat` sizes are not sidestepped or layered in later: "I don't know [that] we can sidestep the nat issue. That is a central design point that they are using." So the array fork and the `nat` fork are taken together: sized types as the team designed them, the checker taught `nat` parameters, in the library's own patterns.
- 2026-09-21, the library route, recorded as decided on his words rather than re-asked: on 2026-09-20 14:39 "I fully believe that the compiler second library is just a bootstrap and we need to get rid of it. Like, I don't even think that is a question that's worth deliberating about alternatives", and on 2026-09-21, when the coordinator listed it as still open, "What decisions are there to make that we didn't already make?" So: one library, the interpreter's (`FortressLibrary` + `FortressBuiltin`), becomes the library the compiler checks; from now no declaration goes into the compiler's prelude (`CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerBuiltin`, `CompilerAlgebra`), and the remaining prelude-name rungs on the ladder stop while code-generator rungs continue; the three prelude files are deleted at the switch-over and their tests kept. How the checker is brought to accept the library — the exclusion sites, `nat`, the first step's shape (he questioned the error count as a gate stage), the order — is a plan put to him step by step, not a decision to re-ask.
- 2026-09-21, on the `nat` plan (`reviews/nat-checking-plan.md` § c) after lessons one and two: decision one, a size left unknown after inference — "the middle is a clear winner": an unknown size is an error only when it reaches a type, a name or a value, and nothing otherwise (the array review's E2); the six api declarations with dead sizes therefore pass, and deleting those parameters (E3) is shown to him as a diff later. Decision two, how the checker represents an unknown size (a new syntax-tree node with its 353,000-line regeneration, or a reserved-name reuse of the existing node), he did not see as his; the shadow uses the reserved name and the real edit's choice comes after it. And the shadow itself: "let's run the shadow test" — the `nat` shadow of decision F, questions 1-3 (crash location, export checker on the six dead sizes, a generic object with a size in its extends clause stamped and run), is approved; questions 4-5 (storage selection, the loader) wait on decision A.
- 2026-09-22, on planning: "if there are known decision forks, which we can evaluate using probes, we should be doing these during this phase, during this planning phase" — a fork a probe can settle is probed before the batch is briefed, so that the decision is his now and the worker gets a clean task, never a decision left to a worker and reviewed after the fact. Applied at once to the run-time size design (operator-style against a descriptor per literal) and the size-in-value-position piece. The re-approval rows are taken one per message with refreshers (other languages, what makes sense in a high-performance language), not in groups.
- 2026-09-22, a design principle for integer semantics on the compiled path, stated while weighing the shift operators: "we should use Java or JVM defaults where it makes sense, but we shouldn't be shy to correct the mistakes of JVM when seen through the lens of high performance and mathematical precision language", as the designers did with rounding and the sign of `GCD`, "they were running on JVM is basically an accident of history, a bootstrap"; "high performance languages should give you tools to stay close to the metal … Swift and Rust type of reasoning": where hardware behaviour is expressible in bytecode it gets its own explicit spelling, in the family the specification already has for wrapping and saturating; "if the JVM itself is precluding such implementation then I guess at this point in time we should just give up fighting with the JVM". Julia and X10 are the counterparts to compare, beside Swift and Rust.

\chapter{Static Parameters}
\chaplabel{trait-parameters}

\note{Non-type static parameters and static expressions are not yet supported.

The examples in this chapter are not tested nor run by the interpreter.}

Trait, object, and functional declarations may be
parameterized with \emph{static parameters}.
Static parameters are \emph{static variables} listed in white
square brackets \EXP{\llbracket} and \EXP{\rrbracket}
immediately after the name of a trait, object, or functional and
they are in scope of the entire body of the declaration.
Static parameters may be instantiated with static expressions discussed in
\secref{static-expr}.
In this chapter, we describe the forms that
these static parameters can take.

\begin{Grammar}
\emph{StaticParams} &::=&
\bTPl \emph{StaticParamList}\bTPr\\
\emph{StaticParamList} &::=& \emph{StaticParam}(\EXP{,} \emph{StaticParam})$^*$\\
\end{Grammar}

\section{Type Parameters}
\seclabel{type-param}

\begin{Grammar}
\emph{StaticParam} &::=&
\emph{Id} \option{\emph{Extends}} \options{\KWD{absorbs} \KWD{unit}} \\
\end{Grammar}

Static parameters may include one or more type parameters.
Syntactically, a type parameter consists of an identifier followed by an
optional \KWD{extends} clause, followed by an optional
``\EXP{\KWD{absorbs}\;\;\KWD{unit}}'' clause (described in
\secref{absorbing-units}).
If a type parameter does not have an \KWD{extends} clause, it has an
implicit ``\EXP{\KWD{extends} \TYP{Object}}'' clause.


Type parameters are instantiated with types such as trait types, tuple types,
and arrow types (See \chapref{types} for a discussion of Fortress
types).  We use the term \emph{naked type variable} to refer to an
occurrence of a type variable as a stand-alone type (rather than as
a parameter to another type).  Type parameters can appear in any context
that an ordinary type can appear, except that a naked type variable must not
appear in the \KWD{extends} clause of a trait or object declaration,
nor in the \KWD{throws} clause of a functional or object declaration,
nor as the type of a \KWD{wrapped} field (discussed in \secref{fields}).

\section{Nat and Int Parameters}
\seclabel{natparams}

\begin{Grammar}
\emph{StaticParam} &::=& \KWD{nat} \emph{Id} \\
&$|$& \KWD{int} \emph{Id} \\
\end{Grammar}

Static parameters may include one or more
\KWD{nat} and \KWD{int} parameters.
Syntactically, a \KWD{nat} parameter consists of
\KWD{nat} followed by an identifier.
An \KWD{int} parameter consists of
\KWD{int} followed by an identifier.
These parameters are instantiated at runtime with numeric values.
A \KWD{nat} parameter may be used to instantiate other
\KWD{nat} parameters, or to appear in any context that a
variable of type \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} can appear,
except that it cannot be assigned to.
An \KWD{int} parameter may be used to instantiate other
\KWD{int} parameters, or to appear in any context that a
variable of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} can appear,
except that it cannot be assigned to.

\section{Bool Parameters}
\seclabel{boolparams}

\begin{Grammar}
\emph{StaticParam} &::=& \KWD{bool} \emph{Id} \\
\end{Grammar}

Static parameters may include one or more \KWD{bool} parameters.
Syntactically, a \KWD{bool} parameter consists of
\KWD{bool} followed by an identifier.
These parameters are instantiated at runtime with boolean values. They may
be used to instantiate other \KWD{bool} parameters, or
to appear in any context that a variable of type \TYP{Boolean} can appear,

\section{Static Expressions}
\seclabel{static-expr}

\note{Static expressions are not yet supported.}

\emph{Static expressions} denote \emph{static values}.  Conceptually,
a static expression is not evaluated while a program is running, and
thus its evaluation
cannot complete abruptly.  Given instantiations of all static
parameters (described in \chapref{trait-parameters}) in scope of a
static expression, the value of the static expression can be
determined statically.  Static expressions which use a restricted subset of operations can occur as
\emph{static arguments} which instantiate static parameters and
\KWD{where}-clause constraints (described in \secref{where-clauses}).
We define the set of static
expressions by first defining the types of static expressions, and
distinguishing static values from the closely related literal values.
We then describe the expressions that evaluate to the various kinds of
static values.

\item The \emph{static} traits, which describe values denoted by
expressions composed from literals, operators (described in
\secref{constant-values}), and \KWD{bool}, \KWD{nat},
and \KWD{int} parameters; here the type
does not encode the value of the expression, but the value of the
expression can nevertheless be known statically if specific
values are specified for the static parameters.  Also, in situations
where the type of an expression composed solely from literals and
operators nevertheless cannot be described by a constant trait, then a
static trait may be used to describe it instead.
For example, a static expression \EXP{2(3+m)} where \VAR{m} is a
\KWD{nat} parameter has trait \TYP{NaturalStatic}.
\end{enumerate}


The only operation on literals that produces a new literal (as opposed
to a constant) is concatenation by using the operator \EXP{\|}.
One may concatenate mixed string and
character literals, producing a string literal.
For example, ``\txt{foo}''\EXP{\|}''\txt{bar}'' yields ``\txt{foobar}''.
One may also concatenate two natural numerals
of the same radix, producing a new natural numeral of that radix.
For example, \EXP{\mathtt{deadc}_{16} \| \mathtt{0de}_{16}} yields \EXP{\mathtt{deadc0de}_{16}}.

Every literal trait extends an appropriate constant trait, and every
constant trait extends an appropriate static trait.  So every
literal is also a constant expression, and every constant expression
is a static expression.




\subsection{Static Expressions and Values}
\seclabel{constant-values}

Static parameters are static expressions.
A \KWD{nat} parameter denotes a value that has type \TYP{NaturalStatic}
(which extends \TYP{IntegerStatic}).
An \KWD{int} parameter denotes a value that has type \TYP{IntegerStatic}.
A \KWD{bool} parameter denotes a value that has type \TYP{BooleanStatic}.

trait Array1[\T, nat b0, nat s0\]
    extends { ReadableArray1[\T,b0,s0\],
              StandardMutableArrayType[\Array1[\T,b0,s0\],T,ZZ32\] }
    excludes {Number, String}

    getter mutability():String = ""

    shift(o:ZZ32): Array[\T,ZZ32\] =
        if o=0 then
            self
        else
            __subarray(self,reflect(o),N[\s0\],N[\b0\],1)
        end

    opr[r: Range[\ZZ32\]] : Array[\T,ZZ32\] = do
        r' = self.bounds.narrowToRange(r) (*'*)
        s = reflect( |r'| )   (*'*)
        l = reflect(r'.left.get) (*'*)
        m = r'.stride         (*'*)
        __subarray(self,N[\0\],s,l,m)
      end
    opr[_:TrivialOpenRange] : Array1[\T,0,s0\] =
        subarray[\0,s0,b0\](1)

    (** subarray selects a subarray of this array based on static parameters.
        b#s are the new bounds of the array; o is
        the index of the subarray within the current array. **)
    subarray[\nat b, nat s, nat o\](m:ZZ32):Array1[\T, b, s\] = do
      boundsCheck = self.bounds.narrowToRange(o::m#s)
      __SimpleSubArray1[\T,b,s,b0,s0\](self,o-b0,m)
    end

content.content:
### Git-history caveat for this map

`git log -- <dir>` is unusable for dating anything: the Mercurial-to-git
conversion behind `sirinath/fortress`, of which this repository is a fork,
cut 146 parent links, leaving parentless full-tree snapshot roots at which
path-limited history from HEAD dead-ends instead of reaching 2007 (see
`explorations/coordinator/lineage.md`). Use `git log --follow` on individual files
(that is how the Feb 2009 start of the Scala type checker was confirmed).

## Git archaeology techniques

- **The history has a parallel root**: `5a68404` (David Chase, 2012-07-19,
  4372 files) is a parentless import later merged by `575fe64`. Any
  `git log <base>..HEAD -- <file>` therefore lists `5a68404` for almost
  every file — useless for "who changed what since June". Use **content
  comparison** instead: `git diff --quiet <base> HEAD -- <file>` and
  `git show <base>:<file> | cmp - <other-tree>/<file>`.
- The twelve pre-2016 branches are hg named-branch relics; the 2008 research
  branches were squash-merged into trunk, so fine-grained authorship exists
  only on the branch heads. Full survey with per-branch verdicts: see the
  session notes / ask before deleting anything.
- hg conversion quirks: empty "Starting/Closing branch X" marker commits;
  `.hgignore` still in tree; David Chase's 2012-01-20 branch-closing sweep.

## Environment gotchas (cloud container)

- Current rung JDK 25 (`/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64`; 8/11/17/21 also
  gated green); `unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` or the proxy's trust-store flags
  pollute every JVM fork.
- `web.archive.org` and `labs.oracle.com` are blocked by network policy —
  research PDFs must be uploaded into the session by Pavol. Archived *pages*
  (not PDFs) can be read via the pure.md relay; see the method note in
  `research/extracts/fortress-websites-wayback.md`.
- Gitignored files (e.g. `research/decks/*.pdf`) do not survive the
  container; only commits and pushes persist.

<!-- A design brief for Pavol's route decision on the compiled checker's multiple instantiation exclusion, written 2026-09-24 on the top tier by his permission, from the notes of 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-23 named here and from `coordinator/POSITIONS.md`; nothing in it was measured or probed, and every number is a note's. Notes: the ground `explorations/reviews/multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md`; the stop `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-exclusion-relax/REPORT.md`; and, under `explorations/reviews/mie-probes/`, `dispatch-and-route-c.md`, `spec-sentences-dated.md`, `price-keep-the-rule.md`, `scope-call-site-dispatch.md`, `literature.md` and `patents-forest-rule.md`. A citation names the note by its basename and section. -->

# The exclusion fork: a design brief for the route decision

## 1. The decision in plain words

- A **generic** is a type with a parameter, `List[\T\]`; an **instantiation** fills the parameter, `List[\ZZ\]`. The rule at issue, the designers' **multiple instantiation exclusion**, says no type may be two different instantiations of one generic at once: nothing may be both a `List[\String\]` and a `List[\ZZ\]` (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 1`).
- The designers adopted it in 2010-2011 to make one shortcut safe. Fortress lets a generic function have a special version for one instantiation, `tail[\X\](x: List[\X\])` beside `tail(x: List[\ZZ\])`, and compiled code picks between them at run time by the value's type. If one value could be both instantiations, the special version could run for a caller who was promised the other type, and the program would go wrong with no type error. The rule forbids such a value, and the checker's return type rule trusts that (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 1-2`).
- The collision: the library's numbers nest. `ZZ32` is inside `ZZ64`, inside `ZZ`, inside `QQ`, inside `RR64`, inside `Number`, and each level says "I am `Equality` at my own type" (and ordering, min, max). So one `ZZ32` is `Equality` at five instantiations at once, which is exactly what the rule forbids. 61 of the checker's 103 errors on the interpreter's library are this, at 23 declarations (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 5`).
- Why it is on the critical path: one library, the interpreter's, is to become the library the compiler checks (`POSITIONS.md:46`). The checker refuses its tower. Rung P relaxed the check alone and found that a program then type-checks and dies at run time, so the relaxation by itself is no fix (`REPORT.md`, "The stop"). One of three things has to give: the rule, the tower's nesting, or the shortcut.
- What every route shares: the `DistributesOver` markers go, since they are read nowhere; B and C both need the call-site fix; and the two code-generator defects and the overloading checker's blindness to symbolic operators are holes under every route (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 2c`; `patents-forest-rule.md § 3`; `scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 4-5`).
- Route A, keep the rule and flatten the tower to the compiler prelude's shape: no checker work, 14 library headers rewritten, 367 places that rely on the nesting, the interpreter taught coercion (150-200 lines); the error count goes 103 to 22 (`price-keep-the-rule.md`, the short answer).
- Route B, drop the rule, make the code generator take a generic's instantiation from the call site (43 lines), and forbid the shortcut by enforcing the specification's overload sentence: 179 library pairs and 12 tests refused under the narrower reading; the count goes 103 to 24 (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md`, the answer; `patents-forest-rule.md § 4`).
- Route C, the forest rule of the group's 2012 patents: keep the rule for ordinary generics and let a self-typed trait be carried at several instantiations when they line up by subtyping; about 30 checker lines measured, 40 to 70 derived, dispatch changes unsized, seven library declarations completed; the count goes 103 to 37 (`patents-forest-rule.md § 4`, the routes).
- A reader who stops here is choosing between: making the library's numbers look like Java's (A); making the compiler follow the specification's model and giving up the specialisation shortcut (B); or building the type group's unpublished refinement that keeps everything (C).

## 2. The nine steps, compressed

### 2.1 The refresher

- A **self-typed trait** takes its own subject as the parameter: `trait Equality[\T extends Equality[\T\]\]`, so `ZZ32 extends Equality[\ZZ32\]` says "a ZZ32 can be compared with a ZZ32". The algebra traits (`Equality`, the orders, `StandardMin`/`Max`/`MinMax`, `Integral`) all have this shape (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 5`).
- **Dispatch** is choosing at run time which declaration of an overloaded name runs. A **static argument** is the type the checker fills a generic's parameter with at one call; the **call site** is that place in the program. The **return type rule** says a more specific overload's result must fit the less specific one's (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 1`; `multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md`, terms).
- **Coercion** is a declared conversion the compiler inserts when no declaration applies without it, `ZZ64` declaring `coerce(z: ZZ32)`; the specification uses it between machine widths and resolves it statically (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 3-4`).

### 2.2 What each path does today, measured

- Compiled: refuses the double membership with four errors; accepts the specialised overload and dispatches it correctly; and its return type rule solves for one instantiation only, which is sound only under the rule (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 2`). With the check relaxed, `ProbeMIEPick` links and dies with `IncompatibleClassChangeError` under every placement (`REPORT.md`, "Measured").
- Compiled, where a generic gets its instantiation: at the call site when nothing can be dispatched, from the run-time value when it can, and the value records one instantiation per generic, the last listed (`dispatch-and-route-c.md § 1`). Two code-generator defects were found beside this, neither involving double membership: a cast to an uninstantiated return type, and `ZZ32` spelled two ways (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 4`).
- Interpreter: accepts the double membership, picks the first-listed instantiation from the run-time value, and can fail at the next typed binding; refuses the Naden-shaped specialisation at load ("non-ground types need exclusion"); on the tower the value's own level wins (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 3`).
- Interpreter, on overload sets: its check depends on the names of static parameters, refusing `ScopeArms` (one generic names `Y`) and loading `ScopeArmsX` (both name `X`); on the latter it answers from the run-time value where the compiled path answers from the call site (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 6`).
- So the two paths took opposite sides of the trade, and either side alone is sound; rung P's relaxation combined the two unsound halves (`REPORT.md`, the table).

### 2.3 What the specification says, dated

- It allows the double membership: exclusion is the smallest relation with the listed properties, none of them about instantiations (`Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:184-189`); "trait declarations are allowed to extend other instantiations of themselves", with `Empty extends List[\T\]` (`basic/trait-parameters.tex:339-397`). It forbids the shortcut: overloads may not differ in static parameters, and "static parameters do not enter into the determination of which declarations are applicable" (`basic/overloading.tex:100-107`). It fixes static arguments at the call site (`trait-parameters.tex:374`), yet one sentence has them inferred before applicability for dynamic calls, citing an empty chapter (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 6`).
- Dated: all four passages are 2008-2009 text, last touched by Sukyoung Ryu no later than 2009-11-06 and byte-identical to the 2012 HEAD; the overload sentence predates the rule's entry into the checker (2010-05-28) by a year and was never revised after. The one passage that moved in 2010 is the advanced chapter's Meet Rule preamble, its author lost in the cut history. `Specification-1.0-frozen/` is not an independent snapshot for three of the files (`spec-sentences-dated.md § 1-5`).
- On `typecase`: the specification has no "unreachable clause" error, so the checker's refusal of a clause as unreachable is sound exactly when its exclusion question is; under the specification's relation `ProbeTypecaseMIE`'s clause is reachable, and walk reaches it (`REPORT.md`, "The specification, read around every line cited").
- Between machine widths the specification's mechanism is coercion, not subtyping: no sentence makes `ZZ32` a subtype of `ZZ64`, and its one example declares `ZZ64 coerce(z: ZZ32)`. What it does state as subtyping is ℤ inside ℚ inside ℝ (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 4`).

### 2.4 Where it sits in the tower

- Today: `ZZ32 <: ZZ64 <: ZZ <: AnyIntegral <: QQ <: RR64 <: Number`, each level carrying the self-typed traits at its own type, and `Number` itself carrying four at `Number`; so every level adds an instantiation, and `ZZ32` has `Equality` at `Number`, `QQ`, `ZZ`, `ZZ64` and `ZZ32` (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 5`).
- The 61 errors by family: tower 13 declarations, comparisons 4, `Maybe` 4, reductions 2; ten of the 23 are objects that only inherit the conflict (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 5`). The tower's, the comparisons' and `Maybe`'s chains all follow declared subtyping; only the reductions' markers do not (`patents-forest-rule.md § 2`).
- Row 330 leans on the nesting: "ℤ sits under ℚ under ℝ64 in the tower, so an integer result goes back into float arithmetic by promotion" (`POSITIONS.md:49`).

### 2.5 What the library already does

- Two deliberate double memberships: the tower's self-typed traits, and the reductions' markers, `SumReduction` under "Hack to permit any Number to work non-parametrically" with `DistributesOver` at several instantiations (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 5`). The markers are read nowhere; their only reader is commented out (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 2c`).
- The compiler prelude, the team's own compiled-world library, stayed inside the rule by flattening: Guy Steele commented out the comparison `extends` clauses on 2011-07-15, `ZZ32` and `ZZ64` were siblings under a `Number` without algebra by 2011-07-22, and widening is 15 `coerce` lines with no coercion from an integer into a float (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 5, § 7`; `price-keep-the-rule.md § 1`). `Library/CompilerAlgebra.fsi:16, :24` spell `Equality` and `StandardTotalOrder` with `comprises T`, the patents' self-typed form (`patents-forest-rule.md § 2`).
- The compiled side's own tests widen by coercion and never by hand (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 3`). The interpreter has no coercion at all (`coordinator/FACTS.md:52`); the team left "TODO add checks for COERCE" at its dispatch site, and its phase order already lifts every `coerce` into a callable function (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 3`).
- Where the designers departed from Java: reified generics with run-time dispatch over them. Java's rule exists for erasure, not for dispatch, and the OOPSLA paper borrowed the rule without that reason (`literature.md § 5`). Naden's hole opens only in Fortress's combination (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 6`).
- The team's own way past a conflict the checker refuses, an open level with a `NOT YET` comment and hand-written excludes, was tested for the `AnyIntegral` closure and does not carry the float operators (`POSITIONS.md:45`, `:48`); it is not a fourth route here.

### 2.6 The peers, by family

- JVM languages: Java, Kotlin and Scala forbid the double membership and have flat numbers with widening; Java's stated reason is erasure (`literature.md § 5`). X10 follows Java's rule, its numbers are structs, widening is an implicit chain, overloads are chosen statically (`literature.md § 3`).
- Static-resolution languages: C#, F#, Rust and Haskell allow the double membership and choose instances and overloads at compile time; their numbers are flat (C#'s `INumber<TSelf>` on sibling structs). Swift cannot even write two conformances, and its integer proposal "does not solve the integer promotion problem" (`literature.md § 5-6`).
- Julia: single inheritance, concrete types final, `Int32` not below `Int64`, mixing by promotion, and "no notion of soundness" (`literature.md § 2`). Cecil, the multiple-dispatch ancestor, erases type arguments from dispatch and keeps the algebra at the root only (`literature.md § 4`).
- The Fortress group after 2012: the Welterweight draft (2012) states the rule as an ancestors meet rule with its self-typed dispatch step commented out; POPL 2019 (Park, Hong, Steele, Ryu) keeps the invariant exclusion, checks the static return type at run time, and has no self types and no tower; the 2012 patents' forest rule is the only text of theirs that admits the tower's chain (`literature.md § 1`; `patents-forest-rule.md § 5`).
- No peer nests numeric subtyping with self-typed traits at each level under run-time dispatch, and nobody published a resolution of that or a proof that the rule is necessary (`literature.md`, closing).

- No peer nests numeric subtyping with self-typed traits at each level under run-time dispatch, and nobody published a resolution of that or a proof that the rule is necessary (`literature.md`, closing).

### 2.7 The history, dated

- 2008-05-06, Maessen: `ZZ32 extends { StandardTotalOrder[\ZZ32\], ZZ64 }`; 2008-07-02: `Integral` becomes parametric; 2008-07-15: `ZZ32 extends { ZZ64, Integral[\ZZ32\] }`, the double membership is in; 2008-07-21: `NN32`, `NN64`, `QQ` added and `AnyIntegral extends QQ` (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 7`; `library-scalar-extension-review.md:281-287`).
- By 2009-11-06, Ryu: the five spec passages in their final form (`spec-sentences-dated.md § 5`).
- 2010-05-28, Hilburn: exclusion of two instantiations of one invariant generic enters the checker; 2010-07-26: extended to all ancestors as `checkP`, "as described in the paper" (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 7`). 2010: the advanced Meet Rule preamble rewritten (`spec-sentences-dated.md § 3`).
- 2011-07-15 and 2011-07-22, Steele: the compiler prelude's tower made flat (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 7`). 2011-08-12: the OOPSLA paper's exclusion text (`REPORT.md`, "What the record did not have"). 2011-11-10, Naden's workshop paper: specialisation motivated by the library, the exclusion assumed (`literature.md § 1`).
- 2012-01-20: `CompilerAlgebra` spells `comprises T`; 2012-06-06, Steele: a comprises-based subtyping rule commented out, "Gets a stack overflow error" (`patents-forest-rule.md § 2, § 4`). 2012: the Welterweight draft submitted to OOPSLA (`literature.md § 1`). 2012-07-19: the import root that holds `checkP` (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 7`).
- 2012-08-31, the last day: Naden's write-up, "more work needs to be done ... the numerical hierarchy", and the four patents filed with the forest rule (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 1`; `patents-forest-rule.md § 1`). 2019: POPL, the rule kept, self types gone (`literature.md § 1`).

### 2.8 The derivation from his principles

- Finish the designers' intent (`POSITIONS.md:24`): they built both the rule (compiler, 2010-2012) and the nested tower (library, 2008, kept to the end) and never reconciled them; Naden left it open, Steele flattened for the compiled world, the patents sketched a way to keep both. There is no one intent to finish; there are two implemented halves and one unimplemented sketch.
- Implementation reality outweighs the early spec (`POSITIONS.md:80`): the overload sentence is 2009 text, never revised, enforced by neither path; it is the weakest fact here, and route B rests on it. The rule is implemented and published. But the tower's nesting is implementation reality too, and the interpreter, also theirs, ran it for four years.
- JVM defaults where sensible, corrected for a high-performance, mathematically honest language (`POSITIONS.md:72`): the JVM default is the flat tower (an `int` is not a `long`), and Swift, Rust, Julia and X10, his named counterparts, all take it with explicit or coerced widening. The honest mathematics, ℤ inside ℚ inside ℝ, survives as coercion under A and as subtyping under B and C. On the JVM a compiled `ZZ32` is already a boxed class (`FZZ32`), so unboxing is the code generator's static-type work under every route (reasoning, not measured).
- One library (`POSITIONS.md:46`): A keeps the interpreter's library as the one library but gives its tower the prelude's shape, and the judge struck A for that (`multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md § 8`); B and C leave the shape alone. The decision as recorded was to delete the prelude, not to refuse every choice it made.
- `double[]` and sizes not sidestepped (`POSITIONS.md:41`): mostly orthogonal. A makes the specification's bound `T extends AdditiveGroup[\T\]` usable on `RR64`, which the shipped tower fails (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 4`; `coordinator/FACTS.md:99`); B's call-site fix guards `nat` parameters out (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 3`). C4's `T extends Number` stays valid under every route.
- The library's own practice is the standard (`POSITIONS.md:40`): the practice is the nesting, and A ends it; B and C keep it. microGPT: 37 sites rely on the nesting, all through `Number`'s catch-alls, 7 mixing an integer with a float; under A they need coercion or `asFloat`, and under B and C the model's text changes nowhere (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 4`).
- Interpreter performance is irrelevant to every decision (`POSITIONS.md:38`): no route is argued from speed here; microGPT's 941K calls through `Number`'s `+` at one line are an interpreter count and carry no weight (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 4`).

## 3. The three routes, priced from the notes

### Route A: keep the rule, flatten the tower

- Checker: nothing. The count goes 103 to 22, 82 errors gone (61 exclusion, 2 `comprises`, 19 in `RangeInternals` by a mechanism not traced) and 1 new; still masked at `FortressLibrary.fsi:2526` and never reaching the component (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 5`). The tripwire test `XXXExclusionRelaxRungP` is deleted in the same change (`REPORT.md`, "The three homes").
- Code generator: nothing this route requires; the two side defects stay.
- Library: 14 declaration headers (58 lines in the `.fsi`, 62 in the `.fss`, one in each `FortressBuiltin` file); `Number` gives up 52 api declarations and 57 bodies and `RR64` takes its own arithmetic on; 15 inherited methods restated on the leaves (24 method-leaf pairs); `SUM` and `PROD` rewritten, three options open; the `DistributesOver` markers dropped; `AnyIntegral comprises { ZZ, ... }` becomes well formed and the `NOT YET` accommodation of 2026-09-21 goes (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 1, § 6`).
- Interpreter: coercion called at dispatch and at typed bindings, 150-200 lines in six files, the compiled side's own mechanism (remedy i); or, without it, 160 library and 207 test sites converted by hand and the same in every future program (remedy ii). One line, `FortressLibrary.fss:4121`, is reached by every passing test, so the interpreter rung lands first (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 3, § 6`).
- The compiled side's precedent for remedy (i): of the 40 programs in `library_tests/`, 12 name a type wider than `ZZ32` and 9 bind an integer literal to one, every one through the prelude's `coerce`, none by hand (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 3`).
- Tests: under (i) no test text changes by design, but some outputs can: `x: ZZ64 = 2147483647; x + 1` wraps today because the value stays 32-bit; new coercion tests on both paths; one `typecase` site converted regardless (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 6`).
- Forecloses: the specification's `Empty extends List[\T\]` on the compiled path (any keep route does); ℤ as a subtype of ℚ, which becomes `RR64 coerce(x: ZZ)`; row 330's promotion by subtyping, which survives as static coercion on the compiled path and needs remedy (i) under walk, its unbounded half untouched; "any Number non-parametrically" (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 4`). Keeps the shortcut.
- Not settled: generic inference over mixed widths, where the flat join is `AnyIntegral` (`lo:hi`); whether the compiled checker coerces a functional method's `self`; 212 candidate lines no test runs; the component's type check; which `SUM` replacement (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 6`). And a divergence: the interpreter would choose coercions at run time where the specification and the compiled path choose them statically (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 3`).
- Risk: the lowest share of derived work; every number is from a run-time survey over all 392 interpreter tests. The risk is direction, not arithmetic: the library's shape moves toward the prelude's, and `Number` loses its catch-alls.

### Route B: drop the rule, instantiate at the call site, enforce the overload sentence

- Checker: rung P's 22-line relaxation, in every analyzer, since only the broad placement reaches `typecase` reachability (`REPORT.md`, "What the placement question looks like"); the sentence, 19 lines in `OverloadingChecker` (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 5`). Count 103 to 24 on today's tree (`patents-forest-rule.md § 4`).
- Code generator: 43 lines in `OverloadSet.java`, the arms of a generic dispatcher renamed into the dispatcher's own parameters; `MieDispatchSub` then prints `Marker[Blue]`; the prelude is byte-identical and all 43 generic-overload compiler tests print the same. Not built: generic dotted methods, functional methods, `opr` and `nat` parameters (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 3`).
- Library: under the narrower reading (`own`, a functional method's own parameters) 179 api pairs refused, 11 of them errors already, in families whose repair is padding to one parameter list or renaming (juxtaposition 80, `DOT` 48, `CMP` 25, `MIN`/`MAX` 16, range helpers 9, `__cond` 1), plus six other library files; the interpreter accepts the padding. Under the wider reading (`lifted`) 335, refusing the tower's own implementations of `Integral`'s methods, "which the tower cannot survive". Symbolic operators, which the checker never examines, add 329 pairs by text scan (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 5`).
- Interpreter: no change for the double membership (it already accepts it) or the shortcut (it already refuses it); on `ScopeArmsX` the two paths already answer differently (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 6`).
- Tests: 6 gated compiler tests and 6 gated interpreter tests refused, 3 expected failures too (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 5`); `ProbeMIEPick` becomes a gated compile-error test; `Compiled12.invariantInference` goes red under the `skip` variant (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 3`).
- Forecloses: the shortcut (`tail`-style specialisation), which the specification never allowed and the interpreter never ran. Keeps `Empty`, the tower, row 330 and C4's bounds as they are.
- Not settled: which reading of "static parameters" a functional method gets, the note recommends neither; whether the sentence covers operators and arities; the specification's own two models of when static arguments are fixed; the dotted-method remainder; the gate not run (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 6`).
- Added up here, not in the scope note: the tower's specialised method implementations (`ZZ64`'s `TIMES` beside `Integral[\I\]`'s; `QQ`'s and `Number`'s `MIN`, `MAX`, `MINMAX`) pass the narrower reading and are the inner-level hole the forest probes show, a `ZZ32` reaching `ZZ64`'s body where generic code was promised a `ZZ32` (`patents-forest-rule.md § 3`, "In the library"). The hole is the nesting's, not the rule's, so B keeps it unless it also takes C's completion below (seven declarations plus the derived 40-70 lines) or the wider reading, which flattens by refusal.
- Risk: the smallest measured code and the largest unmeasured reach: 179 is the checker's count of the names it examines, the 329 operator pairs are a text scan, and components and `tests/` were scanned as text only.

### Route C: the patents' forest rule

- Checker: `checkP` lets two instantiations of a self-typed generic exclude only when their arguments are unordered, about 30 lines, in every analyzer, built and measured; `comprises T` on the seven traits in `.fsi` and `.fss` (the shadow accepted the library's bound as the test; under the patents' literal test nothing lifts); the covariant reading of `comprises T`, 3 lines; and a return type rule that checks every self-typed level below a specialisation unless a more specific declaration covers it, 40-70 lines, not built, derived from the probes and from no source (`patents-forest-rule.md § 2, § 4`). Count 103 to 37, the 13 marker errors staying until the markers go.
- Code generator: dispatch made to agree with the checker's static choice under the covariant reading, not sized; and the 43-line call-site fix, still needed on a chain (`patents-forest-rule.md § 3, § 4`).
- Library: the markers dropped (2 declarations); seven inner-level specialisations completed at every level below (`ZZ64`'s `TIMES`; `QQ`'s and `Number`'s `MIN`, `MAX`, `MINMAX`); `Integral comprises I` beside `AnyIntegral comprises { ZZ }` unmeasured (`patents-forest-rule.md § 3, § 6`).
- Interpreter: the probe pair with `comprises T` overflows its overload check's stack; without the specialisation it runs (`patents-forest-rule.md § 3`).
- Tests: all four of rung P's probes behave as under the stock checker; new tests for the forest, the covariant reading and the return rule (`patents-forest-rule.md § 4`).
- Forecloses: `Empty extends List[\T\]` and `Both` stay illegal (`patents-forest-rule.md § 1`). Keeps the tower, row 330, the shortcut and C4's bounds.
- Not settled: the return type rule has no source; whether `comprises T` is read covariantly; which instance a checked call takes on a chain (the compiled checker takes the top, the interpreter and the patents the bottom); the checker-dispatch order mismatch under the covariant reading; symbolic operators still escape the overloading check (`patents-forest-rule.md § 6`; `dispatch-and-route-c.md § 2`).
- Risk: the highest share of derived work. Of five pieces two are built; the soundness rule is ours; no paper published the forest and the checker never implemented it; the team's own comprises-based subtyping attempt overflowed in 2012.

### Hybrids, and the counts that disagree

- The forest for the tower plus the call-site fix, without the overload sentence, is route C as the forest note prices it: the sentence is not among its five pieces, and its overload half is the completion rule (`patents-forest-rule.md`, the routes). The notes hold no cheaper cut of C: dropping the return type rule leaves `ForestGeneric`'s hole open.
- A flat machine-width tower (`ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64` as coercing siblings, the specification's own example) with ℤ inside ℚ inside ℝ kept as subtyping would still need the forest rule for the upper chain, since `ZZ` carries `Equality` at `ZZ`, `QQ` and `Number`; its price is A's conversion sites for the fixed widths only plus all of C. No note splits the survey's sites by level, so this hybrid is named here, not priced.
- The counts disagree by tree and by instrument. 93 to 33 (`REPORT.md`) was rung P's relaxation on the pre-L base `d610695c0`; 103 to 24 (`patents-forest-rule.md § 4`) is the same switch on today's tree after rung L's api repairs; 103 to 22 (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 5`) is the flat library under the stock checker, and its two fewer are the `comprises` errors the flat `AnyIntegral` makes well formed; 103 to 37 is the forest. All four are the gate's instrument, which stops the `FortressLibrary` api at its hierarchy stage. The scope note's 203 (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 5`) is the zero probe's stack, which repairs that stop so the overloading check reaches the api; it is a deeper instr

## 4. Weighing, as he asked

- The premise (`POSITIONS.md:80`): the specification "was written in a vacuum early on", "as a wish"; the type group "knew much more about what's feasible"; "when that wish met reality, then the spec must change"; strong weight on "whatever Naden was thinking and where he was driving the design".
- Applied to the dated facts, the premise selects: the rule stays, because it is the group's implemented and published position (2010-2011, Steele among the authors, restated in 2012 and 2019); the overload sentence carries no weight, because it is 2009 text never revised and enforced by neither path; and `Empty extends List[\T\]` and ℤ-inside-ℚ-as-subtyping carry little, because the compiled checker never implemented them. That puts route B outside the premise: its footing is the spec sentence and the interpreter.
- Between A and C the premise's own facts split. For A: Steele's flattening is the group's implemented resolution of this exact conflict in the compiled world (2011-07), and their last published line (POPL 2019) has no self types and no tower. For C: the patents are the latest thing they wrote (2012-08-31, after the flattening, Naden and Steele among the inventors) and they keep the tower; but they are claims, never built, their self-typed dispatch step is commented out in Welterweight, and the checker's one comprises-based attempt overflowed (2012-06-06).
- Where the facts complicate the premise: the interpreter and its library are the group's too, and they kept the nesting and refused the shortcut to the end; the sentence B rests on was never enforced, but neither was the nesting ever checked by the compiled checker; and "where Naden was driving" points two ways on one day, the self-type bound `add[\X <: Ring[X]\]` (a flat tower's idiom) in his write-up and the forest in the patent.
- What the premise does not settle: it ranks texts by date and by whether they were implemented, and the two implemented halves are both the group's, their reconciliation implemented by no one. So between A and C the premise leaves a judgement, not a ranking, and the judgement below is made on what is measured against what is derived.
- The case for A, as its advocate would put it: every peer he named flattened, Steele flattened, the specification's own mechanism between widths is coercion, every number is measured, and no type theory of ours goes into the checker; the count falls furthest; the interpreter gets the mechanism the team left a TODO for; and microGPT's text changes nowhere under remedy (i).
- The case for B: the specification and the interpreter, both theirs, allow the type and refuse the shortcut, and no gated interpreter program uses the shortcut; every static-resolution peer allows the double membership; the code is 22, 43 and 19 lines, all measured, with the prelude and 43 generic tests unchanged; the tower and row 330 stay as decided; the 179-pair repair is padding both paths already accept.
- The case for C: it alone keeps all three things the group built, the rule, the nested tower and the shortcut; it is their last word; the checker half is built and lifts 48 of 61; the completion is seven declarations and the rule 40-70 lines; the markers it cannot lift are read nowhere; the library's shape, the specification's ℤ inside ℚ and row 330 change not at all.

## 5. The recommendation

Route A, keep the rule and flatten the tower, with the interpreter taught coercion (remedy i) rather than the sites converted by hand. The reasoning: it is the one route in which nothing is derived, every number comes from a survey over the whole test corpus, and the checker, the part he has said he cannot judge, is not touched; it is the group's own implemented resolution of this conflict (Steele, 2011-07) and the shape of every high-performance peer he named; under his premise the two things it gives up, ℤ inside ℚ as subtyping and `Empty extends List[\T\]`, are early spec text the compiled checker never implemented; and the shortcut, which the group's late work was built to keep, stay

- Cost in the project's units: two rungs, each gated on the full suite (a gate run is 739 s, `microgpt-run-c-handover.md:16`). By batch 3's rate, 1.64 M tokens and about 80 minutes per rung landed (`coordinator/climb-batch-3-cost.md:19`), so about 3.3 M as a two-rung batch; the batch 3.5 estimate for two rungs is 7 to 13 agents and 2 to 4 M (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-3.5.md:191`). The library rung is the larger.
- What he would be committing to: the library's tower takes the prelude's shape for good; ℤ inside ℚ inside ℝ becomes three coercions and a recorded spec deviation; the interpreter chooses coercions at run time, a recorded divergence from the specification's static rule; `Empty extends List[\T\]` stays unsupported on the compiled path; `SUM` and `PROD` are redesigned; the `AnyIntegral` closure's `NOT YET` comment and its five-line accommodation of 2026-09-21 are withdrawn as moot; row 330's rationale is restated on coercion with its decision unchanged; the tripwire test is deleted.
- What stays open and comes back to him: which of the three `SUM`/`PROD` replacements; generic inference over mixed widths (`lo:hi`); the interpreter outputs that change when a wide binding really widens; and the two code-generator defects and the overloading checker's blindness to symbolic operators, which are holes under every route and not in the ledger yet (`dispatch-and-route-c.md § 3`).
- What a no to every route costs: the switch-over stays where rung P left it, 61 of the 103 errors at the tower, the tripwire test standing, no library batch that touches the numbers briefable, and the checker-count stage holding its 103 (`REPORT.md`, "The stop"; `POSITIONS.md:77`).
- The first rung to build: the interpreter coercion rung. It calls the already-lifted `coerce_<trait>` functions at `OverloadedFunction.bestMatch` ("TODO add checks for COERCE"), at the single-closure sites and at the typed bindings, about 150-200 lines in six files, with the keep note's `FlatCall`, `FlatOverload` and `FlatBind` probes as the tests written red first, and no library line changed. Today's nested tower needs no coercion, so the gate stays green on it, and it is the prerequisite the library rung cannot do without (`price-keep-the-rule.md § 3, § 6`).
- If he chooses B, the first rung is the 43-line call-site fix for top-level functions with `MieDispatchSub` and `ScopeArms` as its gated tests, since it is measured, changes no gated output, and B and C both need it (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md § 3`). If he chooses C, the first rung is the measured `checkP` change with `comprises T` on the seven traits and the markers dropped, count declared 24, with the return type rule probed in a shadow before the second rung is briefed (`patents-forest-rule.md § 4`).

## 6. Open questions for him

- Is ℤ inside ℚ inside ℝ64 as subtyping, the reasoning of row 330, something the language must state itself, or is coercion between them acceptable as the specification already has it between machine widths (a yes to subtyping points to C, not A)?
- Does he weigh the patents' forest rule, the group's latest text but never built, above Steele's implemented flattening of 2011 (a yes points to C)?
- Does the judge's reading of "one library, the interpreter's" as forbidding the prelude's tower shape stand, or did the decision settle only which files survive (if it stands, A is out)?
- Is the specialisation shortcut something the one library must keep, or would he give it up, which is what B needs and what, under the wider reading of the sentence, ends in a flattened tower anyway?
- Does he accept the interpreter choosing coercions at run time, a recorded divergence from the specification's static rule, or must the interpreter match the compiled path's static choice, which turns A's first rung into the by-hand conversion of 367 sites?

Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.
